ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circle, with four points E, F, G, H marked on the circle. Point E is above the circle, point F is on the right side, point G is on the lower right, and point H is on the lower left. Chords EH, EG, FH, FG are drawn in the figure. The inscribed angle at point E formed by EH and EG is labeled (6x+2)°; the inscribed angle at point F formed by FH and FG is labeled (3x+23)°. Reasoning: These two angles are both inscribed angles, and their two sides are respectively connected to the same pair of endpoints H and G on the circle, so they intercept the same arc HG. According to the inscribed angle theorem, inscribed angles intercepting the same arc are equal, so 6x+2 = 3x+23. Solving the equation gives 3x = 21, therefore x = 7.

method.method_draft: Identify the two marked angles in the circle: the angle at E is formed by chords EH and EG and is labeled (6x+2)°, while the angle at F is formed by chords FH and FG and is labeled (3x+23)°. Both are inscribed angles whose sides end at the same two points H and G, so both intercept the same arc HG. By the inscribed angle theorem, inscribed angles intercepting the same arc are congruent. Set 6x+2 = 3x+23 and solve to get 3x = 21, hence x = 7.
